newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse rally continues to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse rally continues to new highs.

text.p: The ongoing rally of the Budapest Stock Exchange pushed ahead in frantic trading on Thursday bringing the breaking of the 4,000 point barrier within arm's reach, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 3,962.16 points, up 62.41, in spot share turnover of 2.5 billion forints.

Traders said the fact that the Fed left its rates steady on Tuesday was only one factor behind the immense turnover yesterday and today and the market's rally, catching many unguarded, also derived from several domestic factors.
"I think what happened today surprised everybody, although rises by some stocks could have been expected," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
Berecz said he had expected rises in OTP Bank, home improvement product maker Graboplast and plastics industrial Pannonplast.

"But during trading many (brokerages) may have received market orders as investors apparently don't want to miss out on the rally ahead of the year-end," Berecz said, adding that some positive news recently buoyed the market.
He was referring in part to a Hungary supplement in Financial Times last Monday.

OTP was one of the day's most active stocks, gaining five and a half percent to finish at 2,870 forints, up 150. The bank's share benefited from a very positive market sentiment and news of a $50 million EBRD loan to OTP has contributed.
Graboplast rose 150 forints to finish at 5,000, while Pannonplast surged to a new record high of 5,324 forints before ending at 5,323, up 258.

This week's favourite share, chemicals firm TVK, remained in focus after the company confirmed it had asked privatisation agency APV to pay it five billion forints, stemming from the company's privatisation.
